<STATEMENT>

For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). Equivalently, there are infinitely many primes.

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>

First, let \( n \) be an arbitrary natural number.
Consider the number \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), which is at least 2.
By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, there exists a prime factor \( p \) of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \).
Assume, for contradiction, that \( p \leq n \).
Since \( p \) is a prime less than or equal to \( n \), it divides \( (n + 1)! \).
Thus, \( p \) divides both \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) and \( (n + 1)! \), which implies \( p \) divides their difference, 1.
This is a contradiction because primes are at least 2, and no prime divides 1.
Therefore, our assumption that \( p \leq n \) must be false, and hence \( p > n \).
The contradiction implies that there must exist a prime greater than any given \( n \), proving that there are infinitely many primes.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomD [Dia F] (𝓢 : S) where
  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

section

variable [Dia F] [HasAxiomD 𝓢]

def axiomD : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ ◇φ := HasAxiomD.D _
@[simp] lemma axiomD! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ ◇φ := ⟨axiomD⟩


variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomD⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomD⟩

def axiomD' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ := axiomD ⨀ h
lemma axiomD'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ := ⟨axiomD' h.some⟩

end



class HasAxiomP (𝓢 : S) where
  P : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.P

section

variable [HasAxiomP 𝓢]

def axiomP : 𝓢 ⊢ ∼□⊥  := HasAxiomP.P
@[simp] lemma axiomP! : 𝓢 ⊢! ∼□⊥ := ⟨axiomP⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomP Γ := ⟨FiniteContext.of axiomP⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomP Γ := ⟨Context.of axiomP⟩

end

  B (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.B φ

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomD [Dia F] (𝓢 : S) where
  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

section

variable [Dia F] [HasAxiomD 𝓢]

def axiomD : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ ◇φ := HasAxiomD.D _
@[simp] lemma axiomD! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ ◇φ := ⟨axiomD⟩


variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomD⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomD⟩

def axiomD' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ := axiomD ⨀ h
lemma axiomD'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ := ⟨axiomD' h.some⟩

end



class HasAxiomP (𝓢 : S) where
  P : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.P

section

variable [HasAxiomP 𝓢]

def axiomP : 𝓢 ⊢ ∼□⊥  := HasAxiomP.P
@[simp] lemma axiomP! : 𝓢 ⊢! ∼□⊥ := ⟨axiomP⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomP Γ := ⟨FiniteContext.of axiomP⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomP Γ := ⟨Context.of axiomP⟩

end

  B (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.B φ

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S] {𝓢 : S}
informal_statement: A given set of formulas \( S \) has the property that if the necessity of either \( \phi \) or \( \psi \) is entailed by \( S \), then at least one of the necessities \( \square \phi \) or \( \square \psi \) is individually entailed by \( S \).
informal_proof: First, we consider a set \( S \) that satisfies the definition of ModalDisjunctive. By the definition, if \( S \) entails \( \square \phi \bigvee \square \psi \), then it must be the case that \( S \) entails \( \square \phi \) or \( S \) entails \( \square \psi \). This property ensures that within the set \( S \), the collective necessity of a disjunction propagates to the necessity of one of the disjuncts individually. Consequently, \( S \) maintains a form of coherence in its treatment of necessity for disjunctively related formulas.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomD [Dia F] (𝓢 : S) where
  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

section

variable [Dia F] [HasAxiomD 𝓢]

def axiomD : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ ◇φ := HasAxiomD.D _
@[simp] lemma axiomD! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ ◇φ := ⟨axiomD⟩


variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomD⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomD⟩

def axiomD' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ := axiomD ⨀ h
lemma axiomD'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ := ⟨axiomD' h.some⟩

end



class HasAxiomP (𝓢 : S) where
  P : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.P

section

variable [HasAxiomP 𝓢]

def axiomP : 𝓢 ⊢ ∼□⊥  := HasAxiomP.P
@[simp] lemma axiomP! : 𝓢 ⊢! ∼□⊥ := ⟨axiomP⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomP Γ := ⟨FiniteContext.of axiomP⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomP Γ := ⟨Context.of axiomP⟩

end

  B (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.B φ

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩

informal_statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
First, we fix an arbitrary natural number \( n \). 
Next, we consider the number \( N = (n + 1)! + 1 \).
Since \( N \geq 2 \), it follows from the Well-Ordering Principle that \( N \) has a prime factor \( p \).
We aim to show that \( p > n \) by contradiction. 
Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that \( p \leq n \).
Since \( p \leq n \), it divides \( (n + 1)! \) (by definition of factorial).
Given that \( p \) divides both \( N = (n + 1)! + 1 \) and \( (n + 1)! \), it must also divide their difference, which is \( 1 \).
However, the only number that divides \( 1 \) is \( 1 \) itself, contradicting the fact that \( p \) is a prime number and hence at least \( 2 \).
Therefore, our assumption that \( p \leq n \) is false, which means \( p > n \).
As \( n \) was arbitrary, this shows that for every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) greater than \( n \). 
Hence, there are infinitely many prime numbers.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomD [Dia F] (𝓢 : S) where
  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

section

variable [Dia F] [HasAxiomD 𝓢]

def axiomD : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ ◇φ := HasAxiomD.D _
@[simp] lemma axiomD! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ ◇φ := ⟨axiomD⟩


variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomD⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomD⟩

def axiomD' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ := axiomD ⨀ h
lemma axiomD'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ := ⟨axiomD' h.some⟩

end

  P : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.P

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomD [Dia F] (𝓢 : S) where
  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

section

variable [Dia F] [HasAxiomD 𝓢]

def axiomD : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ ◇φ := HasAxiomD.D _
@[simp] lemma axiomD! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ ◇φ := ⟨axiomD⟩


variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomD⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomD⟩

def axiomD' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ := axiomD ⨀ h
lemma axiomD'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ := ⟨axiomD' h.some⟩

end

  P : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.P

/-- The inverse of `MulEquiv.withZero`. -/
protected noncomputable def _root_.MulEquiv.unzero [Group β] (e : WithZero α ≃* WithZero β) :
    α ≃* β where
  toFun x := unzero (x := e x) (by simp [ne_eq, ← e.eq_symm_apply])
  invFun x := unzero (x := e.symm x) (by simp [e.symm_apply_eq])
  left_inv _ := by simp
  right_inv _ := by simp
  map_mul' _ _ := by
    simp only [coe_mul, map_mul]
    generalize_proofs A B C
    suffices ((unzero A : β) : WithZero β) = (unzero B) * (unzero C) by
      rwa [← WithZero.coe_mul, WithZero.coe_inj] at this
    simp

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S] {𝓢 : S}
informal_statement: For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). This implies that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
To prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers, we can use a proof by contradiction. 

1. **Start with an arbitrary natural number \( n \):** Let \( n \) be any natural number.

2. **Consider the number \( (n + 1)! + 1 \):** Here, \( (n + 1)! \) (read as \((n + 1)\) factorial) is the product of all positive integers up to \( n + 1 \). Adding 1 to this factorial gives us \( (n + 1)! + 1 \).

3. **Show that \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) is greater than 1:** Since \( (n + 1)! \) is at least 1 (for \( n \geq 0 \)), \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) is at least 2.

4. **Find a prime divisor \( p \) of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \):** By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, every integer greater than 1 has at least one prime divisor. Let \( p \) be such a prime divisor of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \).

5. **Assume for contradiction that \( p \leq n \):** Suppose, for the sake of contradiction, that \( p \) is not greater than \( n \). Then \( p \) is one of the factors in \( (n + 1)! \), since \( p \leq n \) and \( (n + 1)! = (n + 1) \times n \times (n - 1) \times \ldots \times 1 \).

6. **Deduce that \( p \) divides \( (n + 1)! \):** Since \( p \) is a factor of \( (n + 1)! \), it divides \( (n + 1)! \).

7. **Since \( p \) divides both \( (n + 1)! \) and \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), it must also divide their difference:**  
   \( (n + 1)! + 1 - (n + 1)! = 1 \).  
   Therefore, \( p \) divides 1.

8. **Conclude that \( p \) cannot be greater than \( n \):** The only positive integer that divides 1 is 1 itself. However, by definition, \( p \) is a prime number, meaning \( p \geq 2 \). This contradiction implies that our initial assumption is false.

9. **Thus, \( p \) must be greater than \( n \):** Therefore, every prime divisor \( p \) of \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) must satisfy \( p > n \).

10. **Implications of the result:** Since \( n \) was arbitrary, this shows that for any natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number greater than \( n \). Hence, there are infinitely many prime numbers.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomD [Dia F] (𝓢 : S) where
  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

section

variable [Dia F] [HasAxiomD 𝓢]

def axiomD : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ ◇φ := HasAxiomD.D _
@[simp] lemma axiomD! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ ◇φ := ⟨axiomD⟩


variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomD⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomD Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomD⟩

def axiomD' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ := axiomD ⨀ h
lemma axiomD'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ := ⟨axiomD' h.some⟩

end

/-- For `s : Multiset α`, we can lift the existential statement that `∃ x, x ∈ s` to a `Trunc α`.
-/
def truncOfMultisetExistsMem {α} (s : Multiset α) : (∃ x, x ∈ s) → Trunc α :=
  Quotient.recOnSubsingleton s fun l h =>
    match l, h with
    | [], _ => False.elim (by tauto)
    | a :: _, _ => Trunc.mk a

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end

informal_proof:
To define the class K45, we consider strongly inaccessible cardinals, which are cardinal numbers that cannot be reached by any combination of smaller cardinals through union and power set operations. Specifically, a cardinal κ is strongly inaccessible if:
1. κ is uncountable.
2. For every cardinal λ < κ, the power set of λ, denoted P(λ), has a cardinality less than κ.
3. If α is an ordinal number and the cardinality of α is less than κ, then the cardinality of the union of α sets, each with cardinality less than κ, is also less than κ.

In addition to these intrinsic properties, the class K45 is further constrained by the satisfaction of Axioms 4 and 5, which likely impose additional conditions or properties that these cardinals must meet. After applying these axiomatic constraints, we obtain the class K45 as defined within the given Lean4 code.

As a result, K45 is precisely the set of all strongly inaccessible cardinals that also satisfy Axioms 4 and 5. This definition encapsulates both the inherent properties of strongly inaccessible cardinals and the external constraints imposed by the axioms, thereby providing a comprehensive characterization of the class K45.

namespace LO.System

variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

informal_statement: For every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). Equivalently, there are infinitely many primes.
informal_proof:
First, let's consider an arbitrary natural number \( n \). We will show that there exists a prime number \( p \) that is greater than \( n \). To do this, we'll use a classic proof by contradiction, similar to Euclid's theorem on the infinitude of prime numbers.

Consider the number \( N = (n + 1)! + 1 \). Since \( (n + 1)! \) is the factorial of \( n + 1 \), it is at least \( 2 \), making \( N \) greater than or equal to \( 2 \). There are now at least two prime factors of \( N \), or \( N \) itself could be prime.

By the fundamental theorem of arithmetic, \( N \) has at least one prime factor \( p \). We aim to show that \( p > n \). Suppose, for contradiction, that \( p \leq n \). Since \( p \) would then be one of the factors in \( (n + 1)! \), it divides \( (n + 1)! \).

However, \( p \) also divides \( N = (n + 1)! + 1 \). If \( p \) divides both \( (n + 1)! \) and \( N \), then \( p \) must divide their difference:
\[
N - (n + 1)! = (n + 1)! + 1 - (n + 1)! = 1
\]
Thus, \( p \) divides \( 1 \). The only positive integer that divides \( 1 \) is \( 1 \) itself, but \( p \) is a prime number and hence greater than \( 1 \). This contradiction implies our initial assumption that \( p \leq n \) is false. Therefore, \( p > n \).

Since \( n \) was arbitrary, this argument holds for any natural number \( n \). We've thus shown that for every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p > n \). This demonstrates that there are infinitely many primes.

class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end

  induction n generalizing φ with

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

section

alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end

  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S] {𝓢 : S}
informal_statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
To prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers, we will use a proof by contradiction.

Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that there are only finitely many prime numbers. Let’s denote these primes as \( p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k \).

Consider the number \( N \) defined as:
\[
N = (p_1 \times p_2 \times \cdots \times p_k) + 1
\]
This number \( N \) is greater than 1, so it must have at least one prime factor.

However, \( N \) cannot be divisible by any of the primes \( p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k \), because \( N \) leaves a remainder of 1 when divided by any of these primes:
\[
N \div p_i = (p_1 \times p_2 \times \cdots \times p_i \times \cdots \times p_k) + \frac{1}{p_i}
\]
This implies that \( N \) is either a prime number itself or has a prime factor not in our original list \( p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k \).

Either way, this contradicts our initial assumption that \( p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_k \) are all the prime numbers. Therefore, the assumption must be false, and there must exist infinitely many prime numbers.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end

informal_statement: There are infinitely many prime numbers. In other words, for every natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \).
informal_proof:
To prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers, we will use a proof by contradiction.

First, let's consider an arbitrary natural number \( n \). Our goal is to show that there exists a prime number \( p \) greater than \( n \).

Consider the number \( m = (n + 1)! + 1 \). Since \( (n + 1)! \) (which is the factorial of \( n + 1 \)) is the product of all positive integers up to \( n + 1 \), it is certainly greater than or equal to 2. Therefore, \( m \) is also greater than or equal to 2, and thus \( m \) must have at least one prime factor.

Let \( p \) be a prime factor of \( m \). We aim to demonstrate that \( p > n \). To do this, we will use proof by contradiction. Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that \( p \leq n \). If \( p \leq n \), then \( p \) is included in the product \( (n + 1)! \). As a result, \( p \) divides \( (n + 1)! \).

Since \( p \) is a divisor of both \( (n + 1)! \) and \( m = (n + 1)! + 1 \), it must also divide their difference:
\[
m - (n + 1)! = (n + 1)! + 1 - (n + 1)! = 1
\]
Therefore, \( p \) divides 1. However, the only positive integer that divides 1 is 1 itself. But \( p \) is a prime number, which by definition must be at least 2. This contradiction implies that our initial assumption that \( p \leq n \) is false, and therefore \( p > n \).

Since we have shown that there exists a prime number \( p \) greater than \( n \), it follows that there are infinitely many prime numbers.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

informal_statement: The theorem states that for any natural number \( n \), there exists a prime number \( p \) such that \( p > n \). This effectively shows that there are infinitely many prime numbers.
informal_proof:
To establish that there are infinitely many prime numbers, we can proceed as follows:

1. **Assumption**: Let \( n \) be an arbitrary natural number.
2. **Construction**: Consider the number \( m = (n + 1)! + 1 \). This number is clearly greater than 1 for any \( n \geq 1 \).
3. **Prime Factorization**: Since \( m \) is greater than 1, it must have at least one prime factor \( p \). This prime factor \( p \) divides \( m \).
4. **Contradiction**: Assume, for contradiction, that \( p \leq n \). Since \( p \) divides \( m = (n + 1)! + 1 \), it must also divide \( (n + 1)! \) because \( p \) divides the difference \( m - (n + 1)! = 1 \). However, if \( p \leq n \), then \( p \) is already a factor of \( (n + 1)! \), and thus \( p \) divides 1, which is impossible because any prime number is at least 2.
5. **Conclusion**: The contradiction implies that our assumption \( p \leq n \) is false. Therefore, \( p > n \), establishing that for any natural number \( n \), there exists a prime \( p \) such that \( p > n \). This completes the proof that there are infinitely many prime numbers.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end


class HasAxiomT (𝓢 : S) where
  T (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.T φ

section

variable [HasAxiomT 𝓢]

def axiomT : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ := HasAxiomT.T _
@[simp] lemma axiomT! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ := ⟨axiomT⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomT⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomT Γ := ⟨fun _ ↦ Context.of axiomT⟩

def axiomT' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ φ := axiomT ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomT'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! φ := ⟨axiomT' h.some⟩

end

  D (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.D φ

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

/-- Equivalence between `Fin n` and `{ i // i < n }`. -/

  toFun a := ⟨a.1, a.2⟩
  invFun a := ⟨a.1, a.2⟩
  left_inv := fun ⟨_, _⟩ => rfl
  right_inv := fun ⟨_, _⟩ => rfl

There are infinitely many prime numbers.

<PROOF>

To prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers, we will use a classic argument by contradiction, inspired by Euclid's proof.

**Step 1:** Assume, for the sake of contradiction, that there are only finitely many prime numbers. Let's list all the primes as \( p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n \).

**Step 2:** Consider the number \( N = p_1 \times p_2 \times \ldots \times p_n + 1 \). This number \( N \) is greater than 1 and is not divisible by any of the primes \( p_1 \) through \( p_n \) because dividing \( N \) by any \( p_i \) leaves a remainder of 1.

**Step 3:** Since \( N \) is greater than 1 and not divisible by any of the known primes, either \( N \) itself is a prime number, or it has at least one prime factor not in our original list.

**Step 4:** This contradicts our initial assumption that we had listed all prime numbers.

**Step 5:** Therefore, our assumption that the number of prime numbers is finite must be false.

**Conclusion:** There are infinitely many prime numbers.

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end

class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with

First, let's consider an arbitrary natural number \( n \). We will examine the number \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), where \( (n + 1)! \) represents the factorial of \( n + 1 \). By the definition of factorial, \( (n + 1)! \) is the product of all positive integers up to \( n + 1 \), which is at least \( 2 \) since \( n \) is a natural number. Therefore, \( (n + 1)! + 1 \) is at least \( 3 \).

Since every integer greater than \( 1 \) has at least one prime factor, there exists a prime number \( p \) that divides \( (n + 1)! + 1 \). We aim to show that this prime \( p \) must be greater than \( n \).

Assume, for contradiction, that \( p \) is not greater than \( n \). This means \( p \) is one of the numbers that divides \( (n + 1)! \), because \( p \) is less than or equal to \( n \), and \( (n + 1)! \) includes the product of all integers from \( 1 \) to \( n \).

If \( p \) divides both \( (n + 1)! \) and \( (n + 1)! + 1 \), then it must also divide their difference, which is \( 1 \). However, the only number that divides \( 1 \) is itself \( 1 \), which contradicts the fact that \( p \) is a prime number greater than or equal to \( 2 \).

section

alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

  induction n generalizing φ with

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end

  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _

class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

informal_statement: If φ necessarily implies ψ, then ψ necessarily implies φ.
informal_proof:
We start by assuming that φ necessarily implies ψ, which can be written as φ ▷ ψ. Our goal is to show that under this assumption, ψ necessarily implies φ, or φ ▷ ψ → ψ ▷ φ.

To proceed, we utilize the properties of the ▷ operator, which is defined in the formal lemma. Specifically, we apply the simplification rule 'simp_all', which allows us to manipulate and simplify the expression involving φ and ψ. By simplifying φ ▷ ψ, we can isolate the relationship between φ and ψ in a way that highlights their necessity conditions.

Through this simplification, we observe that if φ necessarily leads to ψ, then by the symmetrical nature of the ▷ operator, ψ must necessarily lead back to φ. This symmetrical property is crucial in establishing the bidirectional implication.

Therefore, by applying the 'simp_all' rule and examining the structure of the expressions involved, we conclude that φ ▷ ψ indeed implies ψ ▷ φ, thereby proving the statement.

import Foundation.Logic.Disjunctive
import Foundation.Logic.HilbertStyle.Supplemental
import Foundation.Modal.Axioms

namespace LO.System

variable {S F : Type*} [BasicModalLogicalConnective F] [System F S]
variable {𝓢 : S}


class Necessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  nec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □φ

section

variable [Necessitation 𝓢]
alias nec := Necessitation.nec

lemma nec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨nec hp⟩

def multinec : 𝓢 ⊢ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => simpa using nec ih;
lemma multinec! : 𝓢 ⊢! φ → 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multinec hp⟩

end


class Unnecessitation (𝓢 : S) where
  unnec {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [Unnecessitation 𝓢]

alias unnec := Unnecessitation.unnec
lemma unnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨unnec hp⟩

def multiunnec : 𝓢 ⊢ □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ := by
  intro h;
  induction n generalizing φ with
  | zero => simpa;
  | succ n ih => exact unnec $ @ih (□φ) h;
lemma multiunnec! : 𝓢 ⊢! □^[n]φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨multiunnec hp⟩

end


class LoebRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  loeb {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [LoebRule 𝓢]

alias loeb := LoebRule.loeb
lemma loeb! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨loeb hp⟩

end


class HenkinRule [LogicalConnective F] (𝓢 : S) where
  henkin {φ : F} : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢ φ

section

variable [HenkinRule 𝓢]

alias henkin := HenkinRule.henkin
lemma henkin! : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ⭤ φ → 𝓢 ⊢! φ := by rintro ⟨hp⟩; exact ⟨henkin hp⟩

end



class HasDiaDuality (𝓢 : S) where
  dia_dual (φ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.DiaDuality φ

section

variable [HasDiaDuality 𝓢]

def diaDuality : 𝓢 ⊢ ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := HasDiaDuality.dia_dual _
@[simp] lemma dia_duality! : 𝓢 ⊢! ◇φ ⭤ ∼(□(∼φ)) := ⟨diaDuality⟩

end



class HasAxiomK [LogicalConnective F] [Box F](𝓢 : S) where
  K (φ ψ : F) : 𝓢 ⊢ Axioms.K φ ψ

section

variable [HasAxiomK 𝓢]

def axiomK : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := HasAxiomK.K _ _
@[simp] lemma axiomK! : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ) ➝ □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK⟩

variable [System.Minimal 𝓢]

instance (Γ : FiniteContext F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ FiniteContext.of axiomK⟩
instance (Γ : Context F 𝓢) : HasAxiomK Γ := ⟨fun _ _ ↦ Context.of axiomK⟩

def axiomK' (h : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ ➝ □ψ := axiomK ⨀ h
@[simp] lemma axiomK'! (h : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ ➝ □ψ := ⟨axiomK' h.some⟩

def axiomK'' (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢ □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢ □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢ □ψ := axiomK' h₁ ⨀ h₂
@[simp] lemma axiomK''! (h₁ : 𝓢 ⊢! □(φ ➝ ψ)) (h₂ : 𝓢 ⊢! □φ) : 𝓢 ⊢! □ψ := ⟨axiomK'' h₁.some h₂.some⟩

end
